items.title: Israel says it dropped 7,500 bombs on Iran in first week of war

featured_image.name: Netanyahu tells Iranians freedom is near as Israel hits ...

items.description:
The Israeli military announced that it has conducted approximately 3,400 strikes across Iran and dropped roughly 7,500 munitions since the war began on February 28, marking a dramatic escalation in the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign dubbed Operation Roaring Lion.[1][2]

IDF Spokesman Brig. Gen. Effie Defrin detailed the scope of the campaign in a press conference on Friday, noting that the munitions total is "twice the number dropped during Operation Rising Lion," referring to Israel's 12-day war with Iran in June 2025. The IDF also said more than 150 Iranian air defense systems have been disabled since the operation's launch.[2][1]

items.title: Saudi Arabia reports first deaths as projectile hits Al-Kharj

featured_image.name: Military projectile hits residential site in Al-Kharj, two ...

items.description:
A military projectile struck a residential compound in Al-Kharj, Saudi Arabia, on Sunday, killing two foreign nationals and injuring 12 others in what officials confirmed were the kingdom's first civilian deaths since the US-Israel-Iran war began on February 28.

The Saudi Civil Defense said the projectile hit a residential site belonging to a maintenance and cleaning company, killing one Indian national and one Bangladeshi national. The 12 injured were all Bangladeshi residents. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier on Sunday that they had targeted radar systems at locations including Al-Kharj, which is home to Prince Sultan Air Base, a key US military facility that has been repeatedly targeted since the war began.[1][2][3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills 2 in Gaza amid ongoing ceasefire breaches

featured_image.name: Israeli attack across Gaza kill 14 Palestinians despite 'ceasefire'

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike killed at least two Palestinians traveling in a vehicle near Al-Azhar University in western Gaza City on Sunday, according to Reuters and local health authorities, marking the deadliest single incident in the territory since the U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran began a week earlier.[1][2]

Medical officials said several other people in the area were also wounded in the strike. The identities of the two victims have not been confirmed. The Israeli military did not comment on the attack.[1]

items.title: Israel strikes Iran's oil facilities as crude tops $90

featured_image.name: Oil surges for second day, Brent tops $83 after Iran orders Strait of Hormuz closure

items.description:
Oil prices have surged past $90 a barrel for the first time in two years as the US-Israeli war with Iran enters its ninth day, with Israeli strikes hitting Iranian oil infrastructure for the first time on Saturday and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz ground to a near-complete halt.

Brent crude rose to $92.69 per barrel on March 6, up more than 34% over the past month, according to Trading Economics. US crude benchmark West Texas Intermediate also climbed sharply, with Bloomberg reporting the biggest weekly gain on record for US oil prices. Goldman Sachs warned that oil could top $100 a barrel if disruptions persist, while Qatar's energy minister told the Financial Times that prices could reach $150 if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.[1][2][3]
